sources.title: Reconstructing long-term settlement histories on complex alluvial floodplains by integrating historical map analysis and remote-sensing: an archaeological analysis of the landscape of the Indus River Basin
sources.authors: Arnau Garcia-Molsosa, Hector A. Orengo and Cameron A. Petrie
sources.access_depth: Full 27-page PDF reused; availability section read
sources.locator: PDF p. 25, Availability of data and materials; Figs. 7/13/15
sources.observation: The 2023 availability section links analysis code and describes commercial TanDEM-X and then-unreleased MAHSA data. That section supplies no palaeochannel GIS download. Current map-portal availability is checked separately in SPC10/SPC11.
sources.license: CC BY 4.0 primary open article; separately sourced commercial DEM rights are distinct.

sources.title: Counter-intuitive influence of Himalayan river morphodynamics on Indus Civilisation urban settlements
sources.authors: Ajit Singh, Kristina J. Thomsen, Rajiv Sinha, Jan-Pieter Buylaert, Andrew Carter, Darren F. Mark, Philippa J. Mason, Alexander L. Densmore, Andrew S. Murray, Mayank Jain, Debajyoti Paul and Sanjeev Gupta
sources.access_depth: Full primary XML and all four supplement files acquired. SI Table 1 visually checked; selected methods, core interpretation and dataset descriptions inspected. Laboratory datasets were not reanalysed.
sources.locator: Main Results: Sedimentary characteristics; Figs. 4–7; SI p. 1, remote sensing and drilling methods; Table 1, printed/PDF p. 53; Table 3, p. 56
sources.observation: Eight sediment-core positions and depths document a sampled former-channel system. Five GS cores cross the Kalibangan corridor; GS7/GS10 younger inset fluvial strata differ from older surrounding strata. Published satellite traces are surface signatures. No ready-made channel polygon was acquired. Spreadsheets hold detrital-grain isotope data.
sources.crs_assumption: Zone 43N is inferred from all core localities; WGS84 is chosen from the ambiguous printed datum pair. Source survey accuracy is unreported.
sources.dating_scope: Source-interpreted stratigraphy at boreholes; no date is assigned to a remote candidate from proximity.

sources.title: Explore historic maps of South Asia with MAHSA and Cambridge University Library
sources.authors: Mapping Archaeological Heritage in South Asia, University of Cambridge
sources.access_depth: Full primary launch HTML acquired; current public portal HTML and search JavaScript inspected; bounded public search queries issued without authentication
sources.locator: Launch news dated 5 February 2026; paragraphs describing 480 IIIF images and metadata for 1,245 maps
sources.observation: The February 2026 launch announces 480 IIIF map images and metadata for 1,245 Survey of India maps. Public historic-map access changes the 2023 access position described in Garcia-Molsosa et al.; it does not establish that the article’s archaeological or palaeochannel vectors are all public. CUDL collection access returned 403 in this pass.

sources.title: Cutch No. 6
sources.authors: Survey of India; MAHSA public historic-map catalogue

sources.locator: Resource 4b28eeb0-04a4-47db-a56c-b3329e6e272b; displayname/map_popup; location tile 62fc21b0-2609-4529-9003-264b1ba4d211; scale tile 8de926d1-e5b6-49d8-8937-fd274c56040c; shelfmark tile baaa8859-ac1a-46e5-85f6-e14389fc3715
sources.observation: Catalogue gives Cutch No. 6, 1884, scale 1:63,360 and British Library shelfmark IOR/X/9884/1/6/1884. Its WGS84 coverage polygon spans 68.5–69.0 E and 23.5–23.75 N, containing the Juna Khatiya/Padta Bet references in B03. Returned tiles contain no scan/IIIF URL. This is historic_map_coverage_only, with no channel geometry or Indus dating inferred.
